# Theory

Speaking frequency counts how often a participant speaks, without weighting
longer turns. [Speaking frequency](../research/glossary.md#speaking-frequency)
describes participation; it is not evidence that anyone disagreed.

Dissent is an utterance that names a disagreement with a decision the group had
already taken. A speaker can disagree and never put it on the record.
<!-- constructs: dissent -->

Proposal uptake follows a proposal past the meeting that made it. It is
independent of whether anyone dissented, and the [uptake](../research/glossary.md#proposal-uptake)
measure is about the group's later work, not about the speaker.

Felt safety is the one construct that depends on what participants say about
themselves rather than on what an observer records.
[Felt safety](../research/glossary.md#felt-safety) therefore anchors the
mechanism in 4.3.
